title: tooling(skill-examples): red when a marked fence re-declares a published type instead of importing it
body:
Fixes #7646

`check:skill-examples` compiles a marked (`os:check`) fence as a **self-contained program**, so it answers "is this snippet internally consistent" and never "does it agree with the type it claims to document". A fence that declares its own `type ComponentInput` carries a private copy free to drift, and one already had: objectui#7636 documented five ADR-0049 retirement tombstones as ordinary writable optionals and this gate was green on that fence for the whole time it was wrong.

This PR adds the gate's **fourth assertion** and lands today's offenders as ledger rows. ⛔ **It edits no fence.**

## Why no fence was edited

`skills/**` and `.claude/skills/**` are GOVERNED surfaces — agent drafts, human merges. A fence edit here would have parked the gate change itself behind a human merge, so the three marked offenders became rows in the non-governed gate script and the repairs were filed as **objectui#8335**. `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over both changed paths returns `NOT GOVERNED — 2 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched.`

## The census, re-derived on `fedfa3e4a` — ⛔ not inherited from the card

Every `ts` / `tsx` / `typescript` fence in `skills/`, `.claude/skills/` and `content/docs/`, matching each fence's local `type NAME` / `interface NAME` against the workspace's exported type and interface names, excluding any name the same fence imports.

| | card (2026-09-07 filing) | re-derived on `fedfa3e4a` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| exported type/interface names scanned | 2275 | **2397** |
| fences in the corpus | 598 | **602** |
| `os:check`-marked fences | 13 | **13** |
| fences re-declaring a published name | 26 | **28** |
| of which MARKED | 3 | **3** |
| distinct names shadowed | 26 | **26** |
| split by root | 3 + 3 + 18 | **`skills/` 8, `.claude/skills/` 2, `content/docs/` 18** |

⭐ **Lit control**: the census's own count of marked fences is **13**, and `check:skill-examples` prints for itself on the same tree `Marked: 13 ts fence(s) (floor 13)` and `Semantic phase: 13 of 13 ts fence(s) judged, 0 failed`. The instrument was not blind, so the census's other numbers are readable. The three marked offenders are the card's three, verified on the tree (only `QueryResult`'s source line moved, `packages/types/src/data.ts:139` to `:159`).

The card's "3 more unmarked under `skills/`" is the one number that did not reproduce: there are **7** (5 more under `skills/`, 2 under `.claude/skills/`), which is what makes the card's own totals add to 24 rather than 26. The re-derived split adds to 28 exactly.

## The falsification, reproduced — and the trap in it

Run on `skills/objectui/guides/plugin-development.md:92` with the mutation confirmed on disk by anchored `grep -c` counts and the restore proven by `git hash-object` equal to the HEAD blob **and** an empty `git diff HEAD`.

| leg | fence content | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **0** | unmodified | exit **0** — `Semantic phase: 13 of 13 ts fence(s) judged, 0 failed` |
| **recorded miss** | `inputType?: never` kept AND `inputType?: string` added | exit **1** — `TS2300: Duplicate identifier 'inputType'` (twice) plus `TS2717` |
| **arm B** | internally CONSISTENT lie: `name: number` where the published required member is `string`; all five tombstones restored as writable; plus an invented `frobnicate` that exists on no type at all | exit **0** — `Semantic phase: 13 of 13 ts fence(s) judged, 0 failed` |

⭐ Arm B is the finding: the fence is **inside** the judged count, and the gate passed a snippet that is wrong about **every** member it names.

⚠️ **The recorded miss survives into this PR because it is the trap.** The miss went red for `TS2300`/`TS2717` — that is the gate catching an internally **invalid** snippet, which is exactly its job, and says **nothing** about drift. ⛔ A re-measurement that plants an inconsistent lie will conclude the gate works.

## What the assertion is

A **marked** fence that declares a name the **built** `@object-ui/*` surface publishes must either

1. **import** it — an aliased import counts, so `import type { QueryResult as PublishedQueryResult }` and a short local shape derived from it is legal and is the pattern this wants to encourage; or
2. carry a row in `KNOWN_SHADOWED_PUBLISHED_TYPES` declaring it a deliberately simplified teaching copy.

Scope is triage's option 2 — the marked population, 3 fences / 4 names today, 23% of everything this gate judges. ⛔ Not option 3 (converting fences to imports is a per-fence judgement on a governed surface). ⛔ Not option 1.

**The oracle is the published surface, not the packages' sources.** The gate's header already argues this for its compiler: the reader of a skill guide is a consumer who installs from npm. It is also the difference between a remedy that exists and one that does not — of the 26 distinct shadowed names, **25 are on the published surface and one is not** (`NavigationContextType`, internal to `packages/app-shell/src/context/NavigationContext.tsx`). Against a source-derived oracle that row would be red with no legal fix.

⚠️ **The inventory carries its own controls**, because a collapsed inventory would turn the assertion green over every offender at once. A first cut filtered on `SymbolFlags.Interface | TypeAlias` **without following re-export aliases** and silently lost **1167 of 1458** names — every barrel re-export in the workspace, including `AuthUser`, one of the three offenders this exists to catch. So an empty inventory, an inventory that reached **nothing** through an alias, and a `src/` leak are each a CONTROL FAILURE (exit 2), never a green. Every run prints:

```
  published    1458 type/interface name(s) from 46 of 47 package entry point(s), 1167 reached through a re-export — NOT BUILT, so nothing they alone publish is visible: @object-ui/plugin-tree
```

That last clause is a bound this gate cannot close and therefore states: it deliberately builds only the closure its fences import (`--build-filter`, objectui#7811), so a name only an unbuilt package publishes is invisible. Making it a precondition would force every run to build the whole workspace.

## The ledger

⛔ SHRINK-ONLY, keyed `GUIDE:FENCELINE NAME`, each row carrying a reason and the card that owns the repair. Four rows, all measured:

| row | why it is a row and not a fix |
| --- | --- |
| `skills/objectui/guides/auth-permissions.md:59 AuthUser` | section titled "### AuthUser type", then re-declares it — governed surface, objectui#8335 |
| `skills/objectui/guides/data-integration.md:81 QueryResult` | section titled "### QueryResult", then re-declares it — governed surface, objectui#8335 |
| `skills/objectui/guides/plugin-development.md:92 ComponentInput` | the objectui#7636 specimen: a private copy that was WRONG and green for its whole life — governed surface, objectui#8335 |
| `skills/objectui/guides/plugin-development.md:92 ComponentInputControlType` | the same fence re-declares the control-type union — governed surface, objectui#8335 |

⛔ **A row is uncovered debt, never a green.** The summary says so on every run, and a green run that has rows prints a second closing line naming them:

```
Every marked skill example holds up against the built types.
⚠️  4 of them hold up against their OWN private copy of a published type (…) — declared in
    KNOWN_SHADOWED_PUBLISHED_TYPES, so the line above does not say they agree with the type
    they are named after. objectui#8335 owns the repair.
```

The gate's own `--measure` prints the would-be population, so the number stays re-derivable: **10 re-declarations over 9 candidate fences under this gate's two roots, of which 4 sit in a marked fence.** (`NavigationContextType` is correctly absent — it is not published.)

## Ablation — all four legs on the COMMITTED tree, with trap/restore

Mutation proven on disk by anchored counts before any result was read; restore proven by blob hash equal to the HEAD blob and an empty `git diff HEAD` after every leg.

| leg | mutation | file mutated | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **iv** unmodified | none | — | **exit 0**, `4 declared … 0 NOT declared, 0 … no longer describe a marked shadowing fence` |
| **i** offender with NO row | deleted the `AuthUser` row from the ledger | `scripts/check-skill-examples.mjs` — ⛔ **not governed** | **exit 1**, `[shadowed] skills/objectui/guides/auth-permissions.md:60 … declares its own AuthUser, a name the BUILT surface already publishes (@object-ui/auth)` — file, line and name |
| **iii** row whose fence is GONE | added a `ghost.md:1 AuthUser` row | `scripts/check-skill-examples.mjs` — ⛔ **not governed** | **exit 1**, `skills/objectui/guides/ghost.md:1 AuthUser [stale-baseline] … only shrinks` |
| **ii** row whose fence now IMPORTS the name | added `import type { AuthUser as PublishedAuthUser } from '@object-ui/auth';` to the fence | `skills/objectui/guides/auth-permissions.md` — GOVERNED, mutated only inside the trap, restored and verified | **exit 1**, `skills/objectui/guides/auth-permissions.md:59 AuthUser [stale-baseline] … the fence imports it now, moved, lost its marker, or is gone` |

Legs **i** and **iii** ran on the real tree touching only the non-governed gate script. Leg **ii** needed the fence itself, so it ran on the real tree under the trap and the guide was restored to its HEAD blob; the same direction is also pinned permanently on fixtures in the suite, which is what CI runs.

⚠️ **One recorded no-op, declared rather than retried silently.** Leg **ii**'s first attempt anchored on `^type AuthUser` — the fence declares `interface AuthUser`, so `perl -0pi` matched nothing, exited 0, and the anchored count said so. The leg was declared **void** and re-run with the correct anchor; the number above is from the run that actually mutated the file.

The fourth red direction — a row whose **shadowed name changed** — needs no machinery, because the name is in the key: the old row goes stale and the new name arrives undeclared in the same run. Pinned in the suite.

## One existing pin narrowed — declared

`does not build a TypeScript Program of its own` (`expect(source).not.toContain('ts.createProgram')`) becomes `does not JUDGE a snippet with a Program of its own`. The inventory needs a Program; the pin exists to stop a **forked snippet harness**. So it now keys on the act that IS judging a snippet — reading diagnostics, which no fork can avoid and which the old spelling did not actually check — plus count pins so a **second** Program cannot arrive unnoticed, plus a pin that the one Program is the inventory's:

```
expect(source).not.toContain('getSemanticDiagnostics');   // and Syntactic, and PreEmit
expect(source.match(/ts\.createProgram/g) ?? []).toHaveLength(1);
expect(source).toMatch(/export function derivePublishedTypeNames[\s\S]*?ts\.createProgram/);
```

Against the four axes: **business need** — the pin's real subject is the forked harness that produced a false green three times, and that subject is now checked rather than approximated. **Long-term** — no workaround: the narrowed form is strictly stronger on the thing it was written for. **AI-error prevention** — a count pin refuses silently, loudly, at the exact edit that would widen the exemption. **Startup focus** — no new surface; one pin re-aimed, one assertion added, zero new capability.

| `pnpm check:doc-examples` | **0** | `Every covered @example compiles, or fails exactly as its ledger row declares` |
| `pnpm check:doc-fences` | **0** | |
| `pnpm check:entry-guard` | **0** | |
| `pnpm type-check:scripts` | **0** | |
| `pnpm lint:root` | **0** | `32 problems (0 errors, 32 warnings)` — every warning pre-existing, none in the changed files |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | **0** | plus a direct `grep -naP` over both changed files: no hits |
| `pnpm check:comment-mask-corpus` | **0** | |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | **0** | `0 of them published source of a package the release covers … no changeset is owed` |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` (both changed paths) | **0** | `NOT GOVERNED — 2 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched` |

`scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` is **not touched**; its licensed strictness region (the `── Fence scanning` banner to EOF) hashes `2749d53ae3a8df033a53b8d7a354fa7e22ee2d1a17f6ad0c3d61122e904e084b` on both base and head.

## What this does NOT do

- ⛔ **The 18 `content/docs/` fences.** `check:doc-snippets` is opt-OUT, so they ARE compiled and equally uncomparable — the blind spot spans both gates. Widening the assertion into that script is a separate gate-design card over a much larger population, and it lands inside the licensed strictness region. Named in objectui#8335.
- ⛔ **The fence repairs.** objectui#8335, which parks for a human merge.
